parts.text:
The edit was blocked. This is a real constraint of the environment. There seems to be a "yul" plugin that enforces pinned ranges to latest. So I cannot downgrade supports-color. 

Options:
1. Keep supports-color@11 (requires Node >=22) but runtime is Node 18 — the code may still work if it doesn't use Node 22 syntax. Let me actually test whether it loads on Node 18. If it works, fine, though engines mismatch.
2. Implement color detection without the dependency (best, dependency-free). This avoids the whole issue and is arguably more appropriate for a CLI that needs to detect terminal color support—many prefer zero deps.

Given the plugin constraint and Node 18 compatibility, implementing detection ourselves is cleaner and robust. Node 18 has `process.stdout.hasColors()`? Actually `tty.WriteStream.prototype.hasColors` was added in Node 11.13 / 12. So Node 18 supports `process.stdout.hasColors()` and `process.stdout.getColorDepth()`. That's a built-in way and is exactly designed for this.

Wait, but `supports-color` is the canonical package. However, if we can't pin it down, we could just test if v11 works on Node 18.

Let me test importing supports-color@11 with node 18.
